Loss of G1/S cell-cycle checkpoint control through epigenetic CDKN2A silencing drives uncontrolled epithelial proliferation.
Loss of chromatin-remodeling and corepressor tumor suppressor function contributes to uncontrolled epithelial proliferation.
The growing gastric mass produces the persistent epigastric pain that, with weight loss, is one of the two commonest presenting symptoms.
Tumour burden and reduced oral intake give the unintentional weight loss that is the other commonest presenting symptom.
Chronic occult blood loss from the tumour surface depletes iron, which is why iron-deficiency anaemia is present in a large minority of patients at diagnosis.
Liver enlargement follows hepatic metastasis, so it marks tumour progression rather than local disease.
Regional nodal enlargement follows local spread of the primary tumour.
Reduced oxygen-carrying capacity is the route from anaemia to the fatigue this entry records, which is why Fatigue is drawn from Anemia rather than directly from tumour burden.

nodes.description: EBV-positive gastric cancers show dense tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes and a recurrent focal amplification at 9p24.1 spanning JAK2, CD274 (PD-L1) and PDCD1LG2 (PD-L2). The resulting overexpression of the PD-L1/PD-L2 ligands engages PD-1 on infiltrating effector T cells, delivering inhibitory signals that suppress anti-tumor cytotoxicity. This adaptive immune resistance is the mechanistic basis for the subtype's notable responsiveness to PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoint blockade.

nodes.description: EBV establishes clonal latent infection in gastric epithelial cells, expressing a restricted set of latent genes including EBNA1 (required for viral genome maintenance), LMP2A (mimics B-cell receptor signaling), and non-coding EBERs. LMP1 expression is variable but when present activates NF-kappaB and MAPK pathways. Unlike several other DNA tumor viruses, EBV persists episomally in a restricted latency program rather than integrating into the host genome.

nodes.description: EBV-associated gastric cancer displays the most extreme CpG island methylator phenotype (CIMP) of any cancer type. EBV-encoded proteins, particularly LMP2A, induce aberrant DNA methylation leading to silencing of tumor suppressor genes including CDKN2A (p16), CDH1 (E-cadherin), and MLH1. This epigenetic reprogramming is a hallmark feature distinguishing EBV-positive from EBV-negative gastric cancers.

EBV-positive gastric cancers show high expression of PD-L1 due to 9p24.1 amplification and strong immune infiltration, making them potentially responsive to PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors such as pembrolizumab or nivolumab. This represents a molecularly-targeted approach based on the unique immunobiology of this subtype.

nodes.description: PIK3CA mutations occur in approximately 80% of EBV-positive gastric cancers, the highest frequency of any gastric cancer subtype. Combined with LMP2A signaling which activates PI3K through mimicry of B-cell receptor signaling, this leads to constitutive AKT activation promoting cell survival and proliferation.

nodes.description: Promoter hypermethylation silences multiple tumor suppressor genes. CDKN2A (p16INK4A) silencing removes G1/S checkpoint control. CDH1 (E-cadherin) silencing promotes epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Unlike other gastric cancer subtypes, TP53 mutations are rare in EBV-positive tumors. The tumor-suppressor axis is thus inactivated by the EBV-driven epigenetic program rather than by TP53 mutation.
